newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pacific Enterprises, Enova eyeing more Mexico bids.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Enterprises, Enova eyeing more Mexico bids.

text.p: Company officials from U.S.-based Pacific Enterprises and partner Enova International said on Friday they will continue to bid for natural gas distribution concessions in Mexico.

The companies are also considering investments in Indonesia, Australia and Eastern Europe, Pacific Enterprises Vice President John Peterson said at a conference here on "Opportunities in Natural Gas Distribution."
The two companies won the bids in Mexicali and Chihuahua to distribute and build infrastructure for natural gas in Mexico.
"Mexico provides more rapid earnings growth than the one to two percent in the U.S.," Peterson said.

Questions regarding residential demand and alternative fuel competition still need to be resolved, he added. The venture is the first of a series of distribution privatizations in Mexico aimed at boosting use of and developing infrastructure in natural gas.

He told a group of about 150 investors and analysts that the client charge in Mexicali of $1.14 per gigacalorie is about 30 to 40 percent less than what the company's San Diego customers pay. Peterson said the lower charge is because of cheaper construction costs.
"It is going to be a challenge to make money," he added. "Acceptable returns might be difficult to achieve."
He and Enova Vice President George Liparidis shared concerns over competition from alternative fuels to natural gas, such as fuel oil and propane, liquified petroleum gas (LPG).

"It is still to be seen if the propane subsidies will be removed," Liparidis said. The government has committed to dropping its subsidiary on the common household fuel by 2.4 percent and for its complete removal by July.

Peterson and Liparidis said it should begin providing natural gas in Mexicali by July, and expects to take over existing pipelines by next month in Chihuahua. Mexican state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) will turn over its assets in the region by December, they added.
They said the companies plan to bid for distribution permits in Toluca, Monterrey and Mexico City, to be tendered later this year.
